title: Unit – 4 : Session – 2 : SLO – 1  |  Binary Trees
sections: A binary tree can have at most TWO children.
The left and right children are known as the LEFT CHILD and RIGHT CHILD.
A FULL binary tree has all nodes with either 0 or 2 children.
A COMPLETE binary tree fills all levels except the last from left to right.
A PERFECT binary tree has all internal nodes with 2 children and all leaves at the same level.
PREORDER traversal visits the root before the subtrees.
INORDER traversal visits the left subtree, then root, then right subtree.
POSTORDER traversal visits the subtrees before the root.
The DEPTH (level) of a node is its distance from the root.
The number of children of a node is called the DEGREE.
A tree where all nodes are filled except possibly the last level is COMPLETE.
The HEIGHT of the tree is the number of levels.
A node's immediate descendant is called a CHILD.
The link between two nodes is called an EDGE.
